title: Production prompt skim-and-summarize sampling protocol for per-domain calibration packs
creator: Asha Patel
summary: Define and implement a lightweight 'skim-and-summarize' curation pipeline to convert live production prompts into compact, diverse, and verifiable calibration packs tailored to each domain. The method aims to reduce duplicate and low-signal prompts, preserve rare edge cases, and maintain temporal coverage while keeping pack sizes small enough for frequent FP8/INT8 validation iterations.
goals: Produce per-domain calibration packs of 5k-20k prompt examples that maximize calibration signal per sample
Reduce redundant examples via lexical and semantic deduplication using skim-level summaries
Ensure preservation of low-frequency but high-severity prompts (safety/regulatory/tenant-critical)
Make packs cheap to regenerate weekly and fast to run through quant validation harness
non_goals: Replace detailed human-labeled eval sets (retain existing labeled holdouts for final acceptance)
Perform heavy-weight re-annotation; this is a curation/sampling system, not a labeling project
proposed_solution: Implement a two-stage pipeline: (1) skim: generate compact prompt fingerprints by extracting metadata, normalized token shingles, tokenizer-length, and a short auto-generated 64-token summary; (2) summarize: run a lightweight semantic dedupe using summary embeddings and cluster centroids per domain, then apply stratified reservoir sampling with temporal decay and tenant weighting. Anchor exemplars per cluster are kept deterministically to preserve rare behaviors.
sampling_steps: Ingest daily production prompt stream with metadata (tenant, region, route, timestamp)
Compute skim features: token_count, avg_token_entropy (model logits proxy), ngram_hashes, summary_text (64 tokens)
Embed summary_text with small SBERT-like embedder and assign to domain-specific micro-clusters (online k-means)
Score each example with combined score = w1*recency + w2*model_uncertainty + w3*cluster_rarity + w4*tenant_weight
Run stratified reservoir sampling per cluster to select anchors and stochastic examples up to the domain budget
Post-filter by heuristics (safety keywords, obvious templates) and ensure minimum coverage for labeled categories
sampling_parameters: domain_budget: default 10k examples, configurable per domain
anchor_ratio: 8% of pack fixed anchors per cluster
tenant_floor: ensure at least 2% per-tenancy representation when tenant volume > 1%
uncertainty_weight (w2): tuned via lighthouse evals, start=0.4
calibration_dataset_size: per-domain packs sized between 5k and 20k depending on traffic and domain heterogeneity
validation_plan: For each generated pack run: (A) FP32 baseline pass to collect logits and reference outputs; (B) quantized FP8 and INT8 runs comparing logits and top-5 token distributions; compute KL divergence, top-1 label flip rate, and regression in downstream task metrics (intent classification F1, safety-trigger recall). Define regression thresholds and produce a delta report. Run additional adversarial subset from anchors for sensitivity testing.
acceptance_criteria: KL_divergence < 0.02 on median cluster and < 0.05 95th pctile
no downstream task delta > 1.5% absolute for critical intents
pack generation pipeline completes within 30 minutes for a 10k pack
automated smoke tests (safety rules) pass on quantized variants
tasks: Integration with calibration harness and add FP32 baseline capture (Reliability) - 4d
Run pilot on 3 low-risk domains and produce report - 6d
Stitch into weekly regeneration job and add PR check for packs - 2d
risks: Summary embeddings may conflate distinct prompts leading to lost edge cases
Tenant weighting may overrepresent noisy tenants if not bounded
Online clustering state drift can cause unstable anchors between runs
Computation cost of daily embedding can be higher than estimated for high-traffic domains
rollout_plan: Start with daily pilots for three non-critical domains (support-chat, docs-search, intent-routing) for 2 weeks. Evaluate metrics and iterate weights. If stable, expand to top 10 domains and add schedule for weekly pack regeneration. Integrate automated fail-safe: if quant validation fails acceptance, trigger alert and pin float32 model for that domain and activate fallback variant in routing.
notes: Aim to keep the calibration packs consumable by existing runtime quant harness. This design favors frequent, small packs to speed iteration cycles in FP8/INT8 tuning rather than large monolithic bundles.
